name: Stolen Token and PRT Abuse
description: Modern Microsoft login uses tokens, including the Primary Refresh Token on a Windows device that can mint new access tokens quietly. If an attacker steals a token or a PRT, they may never type the password again. Sign-ins then look almost legitimate except for odd device or location properties. Identity Protection flags some of this as 'anomalous token' or unfamiliar properties. Treat those as session theft: revoke sessions and reset credentials, do not just ask the user to 'try again.'
mitigations: Rotate credentials if the actor is compromised
